what_its_for: Selumetinib is used to treat children 2 years and older who have a condition called neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) with tumors called plexiform neurofibromas that cannot be completely removed by surgery. It works by blocking a protein that helps tumor cells grow, which can help shrink or slow the growth of these tumors.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole. Do not open, crush, or chew the capsules. Take selumetinib on an empty stomach — avoid eating for at least 2 hours before and 1 hour after each dose. Take doses about 12 hours apart (for example, morning and evening). If you vomit after taking a dose, do not take another dose — just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time.
dosing: The dose is based on your child's body surface area (height and weight), calculated by the doctor. It is usually taken twice daily (every 12 hours). Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribed. Do not change the dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if there are at least 6 hours until the next scheduled dose. If it is less than 6 hours until the next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with the regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store selumetinib capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the capsules in the original bottle with the lid tightly closed. Protect from moisture — do not store in a bathroom or near a sink. Keep this medicine away from children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely through a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating grapefruit or drinking grapefruit juice while taking selumetinib, as it can increase the amount of medicine in the blood. Avoid eating for at least 2 hours before and 1 hour after each dose. Tell your doctor about ALL other medications, vitamins, and herbal supplements, as many drugs can interact with selumetinib. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and use sunscreen and protective clothing, as this medicine can make your skin more sensitive to the sun.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you or your child experiences: vision changes, blurred vision, or eye pain; chest pain, shortness of breath, or fast heartbeat; signs of skin rash, blistering, peeling, or severe acne; muscle pain, weakness, or dark-colored urine (signs of muscle problems); swelling of the face, hands, or feet; fever, chills, or signs of infection; unusual bruising or bleeding; nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea that is severe or does not go away; mouth sores that make it hard to eat or drink; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Selumetinib may not work right away. It can take several months before your doctor can tell if the tumors are responding to treatment. Your doctor will monitor progress with regular check-ups and imaging tests. Do not stop taking the medicine unless your doctor tells you to, even if you do not notice changes right away.
special_populations: Children under 2 years old: This medicine is not approved for children under 2 years of age. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Selumetinib can harm an unborn baby. Girls and women who could become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Kidney or liver problems: Dose adjustments may be needed — your doctor will decide the right dose based on your child's kidney and liver function. Eye problems: Your child should have eye exams before and during treatment, as selumetinib can cause eye-related side effects.
